Definition: from G404; properly, a recovery of breath, i.e. (figuratively) revival:--revival.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: 'Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord.' It is a recovery of breath, a revival — the cool air after the heat, and Peter ties it to repentance: sins blotted out, and then the refreshing comes.
TheologicalSignificance: The times of refreshing carry no doctrine of their own; their weight is the order — repent, be converted, sins blotted out, and then the refreshing comes from the presence of the Lord.
